patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a compact top header with a small square icon/button at the upper left and no visible full navigation list, implying a collapsed navigation trigger.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close the primary navigation panel or menu for small screens. The current section should remain identifiable when the menu is opened.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not show whether the menu opens as a drawer, dropdown, or full-screen overlay.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The implied mobile nav toggle introduces a disclosure-style interactive region that appears and disappears from a compact header.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move into the revealed navigation and return to the trigger when closed; keyboard users should be able to traverse the menu logically.
patterns_found.ambiguities: If the menu is only an inline expand/collapse and not an overlay, focus handling may be lighter-weight than a drawer-style implementation.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches include a prominent large rectangular field near the top that reads as a search or query input area; on desktop it is paired with surrounding content in a way typical of a search/detail page.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: The field should accept text input and submit a search or filtering action. It may also support focus styling and possibly trigger results updates or navigation on submit.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not clarify whether results update live while typing or only after explicit submission.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show compact grouped text controls in the header/footer-like navigation areas and a small square control adjacent to text blocks, suggesting expandable secondary actions or contextual menus rather than only static links.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If implemented, clicking or tapping the trigger would reveal a submenu or contextual action list, then dismiss on outside click or escape.
patterns_found.ambiguities: These grouped controls may instead be plain links or labels; the sketch does not explicitly draw a caret or open panel.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch includes a large bordered panel near the bottom that appears visually separated from the main flow, suggesting an overlay, expanded detail panel, or pop-up content region triggered from above.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If this panel is an overlay, it should open above page content, trap focus while active, and close via explicit dismiss action or outside/escape behavior as appropriate.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The panel could also be an inline card or embedded content block rather than a true modal.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch has a strong horizontal header/navigation bar spanning the top with logo and nav items separated from the content below, a common pattern for persistent top navigation.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: The top navigation may remain fixed or become fixed on scroll to preserve access to primary sections and utilities.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch alone does not prove sticky behavior; it may simply be a static header.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply relatively light-to-moderate JavaScript, centered on responsive navigation and search behavior rather than complex in-page widgets. Mobile appears to rely on a collapsed header control and possibly an expanded overlay/panel pattern, while desktop exposes more navigation directly and may use a persistent top bar. Most other visible structures read as static content blocks rather than accordions, tabs, infinite feeds, or explicit load-more interactions.
